rationale: Start with a broad organic window to observe all 22 compounds and locate the critical separations while limiting run time. A midrange temperature leaves room to adjust selectivity in either direction.

Change only gradient duration to identify slope-sensitive critical pairs, particularly the late near-coelution. The modestly shallower gradient should keep the last peak near 10 minutes while testing resolution gains.

The late coelution barely responds to slope, so test a substantial temperature change while holding the gradient fixed. Higher temperature may separate that cluster through selectivity changes and create time headroom for further refinement.

Test the lower temperature boundary with the same gradient to complete the selectivity comparison. Cooling should improve the early critical pair and may improve the late cluster, although the last peak may slightly exceed 10 minutes.

Raise the starting organic fraction and narrow the gradient window to spend more time separating the retained cluster without extending the last-peak time. The shallower slope should improve the slope-sensitive pairs, while the changed starting conditions also test the persistent late coelution.

Further narrow the gradient from its lower end to improve the remaining slope-sensitive pairs while keeping the last peak below 10 minutes. The first peaks have enough retention to test this stronger starting condition without immediately becoming unretained.

Use the time headroom from injection 6 for a slightly shallower gradient, targeting the unresolved middle and late pairs. Raising the endpoint to 0.85 limits the expected last-peak time to approximately 10 minutes.

Test a higher starting fraction with a shallower slope to improve the late cluster while retaining time headroom. Monitor the early-middle peaks closely, since stronger starting conditions may compress their separation.

Lower the starting fraction one step from the best method to recover middle-pair selectivity lost at higher phi0. This should place the last peak near 10 minutes while preserving the stronger early separations.
Use a slightly shallower slope than injection 7 to bring the middle pairs closer to full resolution while using its remaining time headroom. The last peak is expected just below 10 minutes.
Test a small temperature increase around the strongest shallow-gradient method. This should remove its slight time penalty while checking whether the remaining critical pairs retain their resolution.

Test an earlier transition to the final hold as a different selectivity lever for the persistent late coelution. The stronger late compounds may spread during the hold, while the faster initial gradient should limit the time cost.

Explore a substantially higher starting fraction and shallower gradient for an alternative selectivity region. This tests whether the middle pairs separate again after elution-order changes and whether the late coelution responds more strongly, with early-peak compression as the main risk.

Test a lower starting fraction with a moderately shallower gradient to preserve middle-pair resolution at a warmer temperature. The temperature increase should offset the added retention and keep the last peak close to 10 minutes.

Test a distinctly steeper gradient for an alternative selectivity regime rather than making only small changes around the current plateau. This will reveal whether the persistent late coelution separates on the opposite side of its slope-dependent crossing.

Test a rapid gradient followed by a substantial final hold, a selectivity regime not covered by the previous runs. The lower endpoint may separate the persistent late cluster differently, though some loss of middle-pair resolution or added retention is possible.

Return to the favorable low-temperature region and test a slightly lower starting fraction than the best method. This balances improved middle-pair selectivity against a steeper slope, with the last peak expected near 10 minutes.
Test one endpoint step below injection 7 to quantify whether improved critical-pair resolution outweighs a small time penalty. This brackets the best shallow-gradient region alongside injection 10.
Refine the slope between injections 7 and 10, aiming to retain most of the resolution gain without crossing the 10-minute penalty threshold. All peaks are expected to elute before the gradient ends.

Test a slope between injections 10 and 19 with an earlier final hold. This checks whether altered late-cluster selectivity can improve the score enough to offset any added retention of the final peaks.

Check a single temperature step above the best method while holding its gradient fixed. This tests whether a modest selectivity change can improve the remaining middle pair without sacrificing too much resolution in the late cluster.

Raise injection 18's temperature by one step to reduce its time penalty while retaining the shallower gradient. This tests the remaining local tradeoff between middle-pair resolution and a last peak near 10 minutes.

Test a shallower gradient at phi0 0.35 to recover the middle-pair resolution lost in injection 8. The higher starting fraction should keep the last peak near 10 minutes, providing a final check of this neighboring selectivity region.

Test a slower approach to the final hold than injection 16 to recover early and middle separations while retaining its alternative late-cluster selectivity. This checks whether a hold-dominated method can outperform the best continuous-gradient result.

Use the final injection to refine near the best low-temperature methods, balancing a lower starting fraction against a slightly steeper slope than injection 9. This may improve middle-pair selectivity, with the last peak expected only slightly beyond 10 minutes.
